title: How advertisers make us spend money
reason: 昨天的课程聚焦团队协作，今天轮换到金融经济与消费决策。本集分析名人代言、自助点餐屏和电视节目如何借助行为规律影响选择，适合联系金融科技产品设计、用户决策和营销机制。练习重点不是记忆生僻术语，而是反复调用能用于解释原因、判断倾向和提出方案的高频表达。

targetExpressions.meaning: copy or be guided by someone whose judgement you trust
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when another person influences a choice: Customers may follow the lead of an expert they trust.

targetExpressions.meaning: a simple way to make a decision quickly without analysing everything
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to explain fast decisions: A familiar brand can become a mental shortcut when we are in a hurry.

targetExpressions.meaning: understand something that may be complex or uncertain
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when explaining understanding: Reviews help customers make sense of several similar products.

targetExpressions.meaning: worry that other people are forming a negative opinion about you
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for social pressure: Some customers feel judged when they change an order.

targetExpressions.meaning: be more likely or willing to do something
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to describe a tendency: People may be more inclined to buy when they have time to compare options.

targetExpressions.meaning: think creatively and consider a different kind of solution
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when a normal approach is not working: The product team needs to think outside the box.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Ben Jones's point: When people are unsure, it is easy to ______ those they consider credible or knowledgeable.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Ben says that when people do not know what to do, they may follow the lead of people they see as credible or knowledgeable.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why can an endorsement work as “a mental shortcut”?

options.text: It helps someone make a quick choice without analysing every option.
It guarantees that the cheapest product is always selected.
It prevents businesses from advertising their products.
It gives customers more time to speak to a salesperson.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript defines a mental shortcut as something that helps us make a decision quickly, especially when we trust the person giving the endorsement.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the phrase about trusted adults: Parents and teachers help children learn and ______ the world.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Ben says parents and teachers help people learn and make sense of the world from an early age.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: According to the programme, why might a touchscreen make some customers order extra food?

options.text: They can consider extra items without feeling judged by another person.
The screen prevents them from seeing the available products.
The screen removes all opportunities to buy larger portions.
They must finish the order in less than one second.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Dean explains that customers have more time to look and are not being judged by a person, so they may accept more upsell suggestions.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Dean's explanation: With more time and no social pressure, customers are ______ say yes to extra items.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Dean says customers are much more inclined to say yes when they have more time and do not feel judged.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What did “think outside the box” mean in the World Food Programme example?

options.text: Find a creative, different way to influence behaviour.
Avoid showing people any stories about daily life.
Use only the most familiar solution available.
Place restaurant food inside a physical box.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The organisation created a restaurant-based TV series as a creative and different way to encourage people to eat together.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What increase in basket spend did Dean Ward say touchscreens were typically producing?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Dean reports that the touchscreen design is typically associated with a 25–30% increase in basket spend.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence uses “a mental shortcut” naturally?

options.text: A trusted review can act as a mental shortcut when I compare many similar products.
I mental shortcut the products before I buy them.
The shop made me shortcut mentally of the price.
A trusted review is mentally a short product.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: A mental shortcut is a noun phrase and naturally describes something that helps a person decide quickly.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) topic—how behavioural science can influence buying decisions; (2) two examples—endorsements and fast-food touchscreens; (3) wider use—the restaurant TV series and your conclusion. Phrase bank: “a mental shortcut”, “be more inclined to”, “think outside the box”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: People often follow credible or knowledgeable figures when they are unsure, so endorsements can act as mental shortcuts.
Parents and teachers help children learn and make sense of the world, and businesses can draw on this tendency through endorsements.
Fast-food touchscreens give customers more time to view products and related extras without feeling judged by another person.
The touchscreen example was associated with a typical 25–30% increase in basket spend through upselling.
The World Food Programme used a restaurant-based TV series in Tunisia to encourage people to eat together more often.
The programme explains that people can change by observing and modelling other people's behaviour, while nudge theory uses small prompts to influence choices.
